    - name: Zero the compiler cache's statistics

    - name: Build the native code

    - name: Build the app host, the test runner and the image comparator
      run: pixi run -e app app-build
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crysta-token.outputs.token }}
    - name: Compiler cache statistics

    - name: Keep the app for the system jobs

        path: build/app/app/edi_app
        key: edi-app-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ github.run_id }}
    - name: qmllint over edi's QML (zero warnings)
      run: pixi run -e app --skip-deps app-lint
    - name: qmlformat changes nothing
      run: pixi run -e app --skip-deps app-format-check
    - name: The app's Qt Quick Test tier
      if: false
      run: pixi run -e app --skip-deps app-test
    - name: The app group's Python tests (tests/integration/app)
      run: pixi run --skip-deps group-app

    - name: The UI test against the one committed image set

    - name: Upload the UI test's images and similarity maps
      if: false
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: app-ui-${{ matrix.platform }}

          build/app/ui-diff

          '

    - name: app-build recovers a build/app configured under another toolchain
      if: needs.changes.outputs.app_build == 'true'
      run: pixi run -e app --skip-deps app-build-recovery
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crysta-token.outputs.token }}
  app-wasm:
    name: "app \xB7 WebAssembly"
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.result == 'success' && github.event_name
      != 'pull_request' && inputs.core_only != true }}
    environment: crysta-sdk

    - changes
    - core

    - uses: actions/checkout@v5

    - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pixi
    - id: ccache

    - uses: actions/cache@v4

    - name: Mint a crysta installation token

        app-id: ${{ vars.ENHANTICA_APP_ID }}

        repositories: crysta

        permission-actions: read
    - name: Build the native code

        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crysta-token.outputs.token }}
    - name: Restore the WebAssembly toolchain
      uses: actions/cache@v4

        path: ~/.cache/edi-wasm

    - name: Install the WebAssembly toolchain

    - name: Build both kits and pack the site

    - name: Upload the site
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: edi-webapp
        path: build/wasm/site
        if-no-files-found: error
    - name: Check the site in the browser
      run: pixi run --skip-deps wasm-check "$RUNNER_TEMP/edi-webapp-checks" tests/system/manual/e04_t11_browser.mjs
        tests/system/py/test_e04_t11_wasm_fit.py tests/system/py/test_e04_t11_wasm_delivery.py

      if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}

files.pixi.toml:
# edi — reproducible dev environment (https://pixi.sh)
# From enhantica/templates; the `verify` task is the repo's full local gate
# (recorded in TURN.md's `verify:` field by the agent OS).

[workspace]
name = "edi"
channels = ["conda-forge"]
platforms = [
    # osx-64 is not built (ADR-0017): crysta publishes no osx-64 SDK.
    "linux-64",
    "osx-arm64",
    # The app environment's Linux: conda-forge's only weston (16.0.0), the UI test's headless display, needs
    # glibc 2.34. Only the app feature selects it; the default environment, the core and its wheels stay on
    # linux-64's glibc 2.28 (the `core-platforms` feature).
    { name = "linux-64-app", platform = "linux-64", glibc = "2.34" },
]  # win-64 returns once the bash-based tasks get platform shims
# The org launcher pin: pixi itself refuses to run under any other launcher version, locally and
# in CI alike. CI installs exactly this version via .github/actions/setup-pixi; the hub parity
# gate proves the two agree.
requires-pixi = "==0.76.2"

[activation.env]
# ONE ruff cache, outside every source and test tree. Same class as crysta's: ruff writes
# `.ruff_cache` into the directory it is invoked from, and a stray cache can keep a RETIRED
# directory alive after its tracked files are gone, tripping a layout gate on a folder that
# holds nothing but a cache. edi has only the root one today; this stops it spreading.
RUFF_CACHE_DIR = '$PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT/build/.ruff_cache'
# Bytecode and coverage data join the ruff cache under `build/`. RELOCATED, NOT DISABLED:
# `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` would switch the cache off and make every run pay recompilation, which
# in a task gated on a wall-clock number is a self-inflicted regression. `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX`
# keeps the cache and only moves it. This is the OTHER half of the same cause: the owner's macOS
# run had TWO retired directories kept alive, `tests/acceptance` by a `.ruff_cache` and
# `tests/public` by 24 `__pycache__` files, so fixing ruff alone left CPython resurrecting them.
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX = '$PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT/build/pycache'
COVERAGE_FILE = '$PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT/build/.coverage'

[dependencies]
python = ">=3.12"
# Pinned to the version the committed pixi.lock already resolves (an unpinned linter makes lint
# non-reproducible — a new ruff release could add rules and turn CI red with no code change).
# The pin targets the locked version exactly, so the lock is unchanged by construction.
ruff = "==0.15.20"
pytest = "*"
# CI splits the system tier into parallel jobs by recorded test times (tools/ci/system-tests-part.sh).
pytest-split = ">=0.11.0,<0.12"
# Owner ruling 67: the shell is pinned like any other toolchain input, so
# `pixi run bash …` resolves the same bash on every leg. macOS ships bash 3.2 (2007) while
# Linux runs 5.x, and edi's CI has a macOS leg. Declared HERE rather than in the linux-64
# target table because that table is the gated, isolated C++ coverage port (clangxx +
# llvm-tools and nothing else) — adding a shell to it breaks the isolation that gate asserts.
# Global is safe because every platform edi declares has a conda-forge bash; if win-64 returns
# (see `platforms` above) this must become per-platform, and the lock will refuse loudly first.
bash = ">=5.2"
# Same class, same sweep: GNU userland assumed present. `sha256sum` is coreutils and macOS
# ships `shasum` instead. Global rather than per-platform because every platform edi
# declares (linux-64, osx-arm64) has a conda-forge coreutils — verified, not assumed — and
# edi declares no win-64, which is the one platform that has none.
coreutils = ">=9"
numpy = "*"
# A compiler cache for the core build. CI switches it on (CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER, set by
# .github/actions/ccache) and keeps its directory between runs; a local build uses it only when asked.
ccache = "*"
# Native profiling of the embedded engine without root — `py-spy record --native` on a child
# process is how the unfolded reflection sum behind that issue was found.
py-spy = "*"
pip = "*"
python-build = "*"
hatchling = "*"
versioningit = "*"
mkdocs = "*"
mkdocs-material = "*"
# Notebook plane: jupytext py:percent sources + stripped committed .ipynb, executed by nbmake as
# the verification gate and rendered pre-executed by mkdocs-jupyter (plotly plots).
mkdocs-jupyter = "*"
jupytext = "*"
# The JupyterLab APP itself, declared rather than inherited: without it `pixi run jupyter lab`
# resolves a Lab from outside this env, so the env's own `jupyterlab-jupytext` extension is not
# registered and a .py verification source offers only "Open With -> Editor" — no Notebook and no
# Jupytext Notebook, which crysta's env (which does carry jupyterlab) offers.
jupyterlab = "*"
nbmake = "*"
nbstripout = "*"
ipykernel = "*"
plotly = "*"
cmake = "*"
cxx-compiler = "*"
ninja = "*"
# Eigen is the version crysta pins and its package config requires exactly: left free, the solve took 5.0.1,
# which crysta refused, and builds silently used a system Eigen instead.
eigen = "==3.4.0"
sleef = "*"
# Explicit OpenMP runtime/headers on every supported platform; the compiler toolchain also pulls
# libgomp on Linux, while llvm-openmp supplies the portable CMake find-package seam used by crysta.
llvm-openmp = "*"
pytest-cov = "*"
# Declared explicitly, not relied on transitively: lib/edi/verification.py reads the crysta
# corpus manifest to resolve a case's pinned FullProf reference, so this is a PRODUCTION
# dependency of the verification surface, not a dev convenience. It was already present in
# the solve only as a transitive of another package, which is exactly how a lever silently
# vanishes on an unrelated repin.
pyyaml = "*"
# The header-only C++ unit-test framework for edi's doctest tier, at the same choice
# crysta made in (doctest, not Catch2 v3 — which stopped being header-only). One binary,
# built EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL by `cpp-test`.
doctest = "*"
# Non-GUI QML expression gates execute JavaScript in this declared environment.
nodejs = "==22.23.2"

# The LLVM source-based coverage toolchain, linux-64 ONLY — coverage runs on the Linux leg
# exclusively, so the macOS solves stay untouched. clangxx supplies the clang++ driver;
# llvm-tools supplies llvm-cov + llvm-profdata. Both pinned to the org major recorded in the
# design records §Compilers. Declare the macOS deployment target instead of inheriting the
# build machine's SDK default. edi declared none anywhere — pixi.toml, pyproject.toml, CMake or
# its workflows — so its macOS floor was whatever Mac built it, silently, and could differ
# between machines. edi LINKS crysta, so its real floor can never be below crysta's; declaring
# the same declaring one makes that relationship a fact rather than a coincidence.
#
# ⛔ THE VALUE IS 13.4 BECAUSE EDI'S OWN SOURCE REQUIRES IT; crysta's source needs nothing higher, and crysta declares the same 13.4 so the two products carry ONE
# target: edi builds crysta with this value, and core-build passes it to every configure so compile and link agree. core/src/io.cpp's format_double calls
# std::to_chars ON A DOUBLE, and in the libc++ this repo compiles against (libcxx-devel 19.1.7) that overload carries
# `__attribute__((availability(macos, strict, introduced = 13.4)))`; declaring 13.0 pinned edi
# BELOW its own requirement and macOS CI said so exactly:
#     core/src/io.cpp:1243:30: error: 'to_chars' is unavailable: introduced in macOS 13.4
# Before this cycle edi declared nothing and inherited the build machine's SDK default, which is
# higher, so the requirement was satisfied by accident and never stated.
#
# ⚠️ This is NOT the from_chars question that reverted crysta's floor, and the difference is the
# whole reason 13.4 works here: to_chars maps to _LIBCPP_AVAILABILITY_HAS_TO_CHARS_FLOATING_POINT
# (LLVM 14/15), a REAL deployment-target gate at 13.4; from_chars maps to
# _LIBCPP_INTRODUCED_IN_LLVM_20, which the Apple branch defines as 0 unconditionally and which no
# floor can unlock. edi needs the one that a floor can actually buy.
#
# 13.4 is also the CEILING of what edi needs, checked rather than assumed: of the libc++ features
# carrying availability markup, the only one edi uses above LLVM 14 is none — no std::pmr, no
# std::print, no chrono tzdb, no std::expected, no memory_resource. The one osx platform edi
# ships (osx-64 dropped, ADR-0017) declares its floor explicitly. The crysta SDK pin (ADR-0017)
# lives in each platform's activation env:
# `pixi run crysta-sdk-pin <sha>` writes CRYSTA_SDK_TAG and CRYSTA_SDK_SHA256 from build-<sha>'s release, or
# from crysta's pull-request run at <sha> while that head has no release, and
# tools/ci/build-crysta.sh reads them from this file. Only an update PR or a paired PR moves them.
[target.osx-arm64.activation.env]
MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = '13.4'
CRYSTA_SDK_TAG = "build-c2b02623e0b8354cec2dcfaeb2939645486c0dca"
CRYSTA_SDK_SHA256 = "ee816121d013e2a9b72ba4e203178c63e4b607119dcda3beee7bfffd3e047721"

[target.linux-64.activation.env]
CRYSTA_SDK_TAG = "build-c2b02623e0b8354cec2dcfaeb2939645486c0dca"
CRYSTA_SDK_SHA256 = "732c2a6ca45090d49f5ba14a453f164e7989ad9ab96d01913624971e2c625079"

[target.linux-64.dependencies]
clangxx = "22.*"
llvm-tools = "22.*"

# ADR-0015: the Qt/QML app host builds in its own environment, so the default environment stays Qt-free for
# the core, the bindings and CI legs that never touch the app. qt6-main is LGPL-3.0-only on conda-forge.
# qt6-graphs and qt6-quick3d are GPL-3.0-only: the app links Qt Graphs for the pattern chart and Qt Quick 3D
# for the structure view, and the distributed app is a GPLv3 work while edi's source stays BSD-3 (ADR-0015
# §6, ADR-0008).
[feature.app.dependencies]
qt6-main = "6.11.*"
qt6-graphs = "6.11.*"
qt6-quick3d = "6.11.*"
# The app environment builds with the default environment's compilers: left free, the solve takes
# cxx-compiler 2 and with it a third clang (21) on macOS, which the org toolchain parity gate refuses.
cxx-compiler = "1.11.*"
# A compiler cache for the app build (about 500 targets, 270 of them QML compiled to C++) and the app
# environment's crysta, as crysta's own CI uses. A hit reproduces the identical object; the cache
# directory lives outside the workspace (CI: $HOME/.cache/edi-ccache), so it survives the checkout's
# clean. Opt out with CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=''.
ccache = "*"
# FindVulkan's headers from this environment on both platforms, never a system or Homebrew copy.
libvulkan-headers = "1.4.*"

# The Linux UI test's headless display (tools/ci/app-platform.sh; ADR-0015 §10): a rootful Xwayland on
# Weston's headless backend, with Mesa's llvmpipe as the OpenGL Qt Quick draws through.
[feature.app.target.linux-64.dependencies]
# The app environment links the crysta SDK, so its ABI packages resolve exactly as crysta's cpp-ci built it
# (version AND build; the org toolchain moves both together).
gcc_impl_linux-64 = { version = "==14.3.0", build = "h235f0fe_19" }
gxx_impl_linux-64 = { version = "==14.3.0", build = "h2185e75_19" }
libgcc = { version = "==15.2.0", build = "he0feb66_19" }
libgcc-devel_linux-64 = { version = "==14.3.0", build = "hf649bbc_119" }
libstdcxx = { version = "==15.2.0", build = "h934c35e_19" }
libstdcxx-devel_linux-64 = { version = "==14.3.0", build = "h9f08a49_119" }
libgomp = { version = "==15.2.0", build = "he0feb66_19" }
sysroot_linux-64 = { version = "==2.28", build = "h4ee821c_9" }
eigen = { version = "==3.4.0", build = "h54a6638_2" }
sleef = { version = "==3.9.0", build = "ha0421bc_0" }
weston = "16.*"
xwayland = "24.*"
mesa-llvmpipe = "26.*"
# Headers Qt's configure looks for (FindOpenGL's GLES2/GLES3/GLU, FindVulkan), declared so they resolve in
# this environment instead of a runner's /usr/include. Build-time headers only: the app links none of their
# libraries, and the Vulkan loader it loads is the environment's libvulkan-loader.
libgles-devel = "1.7.*"
libglu = "9.0.*"

# CMake initialises its compiler launcher from these at configure time, so app-build and the app
# environment's crysta build (build-crysta.sh) both compile through ccache.
[feature.app.target.osx-arm64.dependencies]
# The app environment links the crysta SDK, so its ABI packages resolve exactly as crysta's cpp-ci built it
# (version AND build; the org toolchain moves both together).
clang_impl_osx-arm64 = { version = "==19.1.7", build = "default_hc11f16d_9" }
clangxx_impl_osx-arm64 = { version = "==19.1.7", build = "default_hc11f16d_9" }
libcxx = { version = "==22.1.8", build = "h55c6f16_0" }
libcxx-devel = { version = "==19.1.7", build = "h6dc3340_2" }
llvm-openmp = { version = "==22.1.8", build = "hc7d1edf_0" }
eigen = { version = "==3.4.0", build = "h784d473_2" }
sleef = { version = "==3.9.0", build = "hb028509_0" }

# ADR-0023: the WebAssembly toolchain's Qt kits come through aqtinstall, pinned here; the app environment's
# Qt is the host Qt they need (QT_HOST_PATH). Emscripten is pinned in tools/ci/wasm-env.sh.
[feature.app.pypi-dependencies]
aqtinstall = "==3.3.0"

[feature.app.activation.env]
CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER = "ccache"
CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER = "ccache"

# The app environment runs on linux-64-app (glibc 2.34, for weston) instead of linux-64.
[feature.app]
platforms = ["linux-64-app", "osx-arm64"]

# The default environment keeps the workspace's own platforms, never linux-64-app.
[feature.core-platforms]
platforms = ["linux-64", "osx-arm64"]

[feature.app.tasks]
# Build the app host into build/app (crysta first, through the same build-crysta.sh the core uses). Each app
# step below builds first when run on its own (an incremental build, every time); a full sequence builds once
# and runs each step on that build: app-verify (and the verify chains that include it) through pixi's shared
# dependency, each CI app job through `pixi run --skip-deps` (as the owner corrected it on 2026-09-29).
app-build = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-build.sh"] }
# Build, then start the app: `pixi run -e app app` (arguments pass through: `pixi run -e app app --demo out/`).
app = { cmd = "EDI_APP_TARGETS=edi_app bash tools/ci/app-build.sh && bash tools/ci/app-run.sh" }
# Start the already-built app with no build and no network check.
app-run = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-run.sh"] }
# Development only: build crysta from a local checkout, link the app to it and start it
# (`pixi run -e app app-with-crysta ../crysta`; docs/dev/local-crysta.md).
app-with-crysta = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/dev/app-with-crysta.sh"] }
# Run the app's Qt Quick Test tier with the runner app-build built (refuses a vacuous run).
app-test = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-test.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
# The drawn cases (tests/unit/app/tst_*_drawn.qml) on the capture platform, where Qt Quick 3D draws; by hand while
# the app tests are off, and the macOS runner's `bank_frames` dispatch (edi ADR-0017 §16).
app-test-3d = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-test-3d.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
# The drawn cases ten times, their tables compared with the latency bank's app rows and banked from GPU hardware
# only: the macOS runner's `bank_frames` dispatch, or the owner's Mac by hand (`pixi run -e app app-bank-frames`,
# then commit tests/latency-bank.json). Arguments go to latency_bank.py.
app-bank-frames = { cmd = ["python", "tools/ci/latency_bank.py", "--run-app"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
# qmllint over edi's QML, zero warnings; qmlformat changes nothing (`app-format` applies it).
app-lint = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-lint.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
app-format-check = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-format-check.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
app-format = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-format-check.sh", "--apply"] }
# The UI test: the demo's page images against the one committed set, by SSIM; `app-ui-bless` replaces
# the set with the last run (a reviewed act — commit it with the reason).
app-ui-test = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-ui-test.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
app-ui-bless = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-ui-bless.sh"] }
# ADR-0017 §15: the measured-layer benchmark, by hand: Qt Graphs' own series against edi's scene-graph
# item, on the stress dataset's measured series. Prints one table.
app-chart-bench = { cmd = "EDI_APP_TARGETS=edi_app_chart_bench bash tools/ci/app-build.sh && build/app/app/edi_app_chart_bench" }
# app-build's recovery from a stale build/app (another environment's compilers): CI's last app step.
app-build-recovery = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/app-build-recovery.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
# ADR-0023: the app as a WebAssembly site. `wasm-toolchain` installs Emscripten and Qt's two wasm kits once
# (~/.cache/edi-wasm); `wasm-build` builds crysta and the app for both kits and packs the site zip into
# build/wasm (`wasm-build multithread` or `singlethread` builds one).
wasm-toolchain = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/wasm-toolchain.sh"] }
wasm-build = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/wasm-build.sh"], depends-on = [{ task = "crysta-sdk", environment = "default" }, { task = "wasm-toolchain", environment = "app" }] }
# Every app gate, for verify-quick / verify-full, which reach it through `app-verify` in the default
# environment (so the default environment stays Qt-free).
# Without app-test and app-ui-test while the owner has them disabled (re-enabling is a revert); `pixi run
# -e app app-test`, `app-ui-test` and `app-ui-bless` still run by hand.
app-gates = { depends-on = [{ task = "app-build", environment = "app" }, "app-lint", "app-format-check"] }

[environments]
default = ["core-platforms"]
app = ["app"]

[pypi-dependencies]
easydiffraction = { path = ".", editable = true }
nanobind = "*"

[tasks]
# --- lint / format -----------------------------------------------------------------
check = "ruff check ."
format-check = "ruff format --check ."
format = "ruff format ."
# --- tests --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Exit code 5 (= no
# tests collected) is tolerated so the gate is green on the pre-code skeleton and tightens automatically
# once the first test lands. depends-on core-build: from the suite imports `edi._edi` (a git-ignored
# nanobind extension built by core-build), so the extension MUST be built before pytest — otherwise a clean
# CI checkout / clean tree has no `_edi.so` and `import edi` fails, while a stale `.so` masks it locally.
# The core suites leave out tests/integration/app, the app group: it needs the Qt app build and runs as
# group-app after app-build (app-verify, both CI app jobs; tests/test-groups.json "app").
test = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/pytest-lenient.sh", "--ignore=tests/integration/app"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# The quick (review-time) selection runs the FULL tier set — the measured-`heavy` exclusion is
# retired (tests/test-groups.json declares the named groups, equal on test selection). Renamed
# from `per-commit-tests` — the owner cadence
# ruling (2026-08-28) runs NOTHING per commit; this is the quick group's python half, run once
# before handing to review. The retired `tests/simulation` tier is gone: owner ruling 18 voided
# its rationale, and cross-engine parity now lives at system level reading paired corpus
# references (docs/dev/design/where-tests-live.md).
quick-tests = { cmd = [
    "python", "-m", "pytest",

# The nightly-only group (tests/test-groups.json): files that build an app of their own, run only by the nightly

    "tests/system/py/test_scan_correlation_save_stability.py",

# CI runs the same selection as parallel jobs (owner, 2026-10-08): `core-tests` (unit and integration) in

# times (tools/ci/system-tests-part.sh). Together they are exactly quick-tests' selection, except that only the

core-tests = { cmd = [
    "python", "-m", "pytest",
    "tests/unit", "tests/integration", "--ignore=tests/integration/app",
    "-q",
], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
system-tests-part = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/system-tests-part.sh"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# --- core (C++) ---------------------------------------------------------------------- / item 8: the
# pinned crysta SDK (downloaded or reused, never compiled) and its source, for every prefix reader — also
# in a consumer job, where core-build only restores the native build.
crysta-sdk = "bash tools/ci/build-crysta.sh && bash tools/ci/crysta-src.sh"
core-build = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/core-build.sh"] }  # acquires the SDK inside its producer lock
# Pin crysta build-<sha> for every platform (`pixi run crysta-sdk-pin <sha>`).
crysta-sdk-pin = { cmd = ["python", "tools/ci/crysta_sdk_pin.py"] }
crysta-consumer = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/crysta-consumer.sh"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# Edi-py carries every name crysta-py declares public — proven as EXISTENCE, nothing more.
# crysta's C++ package installs the committed declaration of its public PYTHON interface
# (share/crysta/python-surface.json) into the prefix core-build populates; this gate reads it from
# there (never a sibling checkout, never `import crysta`) and proves every declared name, and every
# declared member of a declared class, resolves in the built `edi` (no signature, default, type or
# base chain is compared — behaviour is demonstrated by crysta's s/crysta/edi/ substitution scripts
# at crysta's consumer job). OK only at zero findings; an absent declaration (a pinned crysta older
# than it) is a REFUSAL, never a skip.
#
# Every fetch delivers a declaration-carrying crysta main, so this gate proves the real
# existence property in BOTH verify chains — the refusal-only era (and the follow-up that
# closed it) is over; the crysta PR consumer job still proves it against each PR's own tree.
python-surface-superset = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/python_surface_superset.py"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
cli-vocabulary-check = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/cli_vocabulary.py"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# Edi's own declaration and necessity record (data/python-surface.json, schema 4 — the same shape as
# crysta's): every module name and every member of every class-like name carries an audience verdict
# and a necessity verdict; drift, an unclassified name, a removed name still reachable, or an
# undecided row is red. In both verify chains.
python-surface-check = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/python_surface.py", "--check"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# --- verification notebooks (task names mirror diffraction-lib) -------------- Authored source =
# jupytext py:percent .py; the paired .ipynb is committed STRIPPED and executed fresh by nbmake
# (the in-notebook FullProf assertions are the gate). notebook-exec-ci overwrites outputs for the
# docs render only — the gate (notebook-tests) never mutates the tree. The .ipynb are DERIVED
# artifacts — untracked, gitignored, regenerated by notebook-prepare — so executing them in place
# cannot dirty the source tree. notebook-tests regenerates its own inputs; docs-build renders
# whatever the CI docs job (or a local notebook-prepare/-exec-ci run) left in place. The
# EXECUTION scopes lead this block — the exclusion gate derives the executed set from these
# nbmake invocations, and the tutorials are deliberately NOT in them (the declared exclusion in
# docs/user/tutorials/execution-exclusions.yml); the convert/strip tasks below add the tutorials
# for RENDERING only.
notebook-tests = { cmd = ["python", "-m", "pytest", "--nbmake", "docs/dev/verification/", "--nbmake-timeout=600", "--color=yes", "-v"], depends-on = ["core-build", "notebook-prepare"] }
notebook-exec-ci = { cmd = ["python", "-m", "pytest", "--nbmake", "docs/dev/verification/", "--nbmake-timeout=600", "--overwrite", "--color=yes", "-v"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
verification-exec = { depends-on = ["notebook-exec-ci"] }
notebook-convert = "jupytext docs/dev/verification/*.py docs/user/tutorials/*.py --from py:percent --to ipynb"
notebook-strip = "nbstripout docs/dev/verification/*.ipynb docs/user/tutorials/*.ipynb"
notebook-prepare = { depends-on = ["notebook-convert", "notebook-strip"] }
notebook-lint-check = "ruff check docs/dev/verification/"
# --- the CLI projects ---------------------------------------------------- Every project in
# docs/user/cli/projects.yml's EXECUTING set runs through `python -m edi fit` on a disposable copy
# and is compared with its expected.json; any deviation is red. The same step runs in both verify
# chains AND in CI's pull-request `cli-projects` job (a gate never lives in only one of the two).
# The whole set, never a subset — subsetting on runtime is the owner's call. First, the app's example index
# must match the registry's project records (ADR-0031).
cli-projects = { cmd = "python tools/dev/example_metadata.py --check && python tools/checks/cli_projects.py", depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# --- the fast per-PR physics signal ----------------------------------------- The
# independent-reference signal a crysta pull request runs against edi, rehomed: the retired
# `tests/simulation` page-executing tier is replaced by cross-engine parity at system level, which
# calculates on a corpus case's grid and compares against that case's manifest-declared frozen
# FullProf profile. Still headless and fit-free, which is what kept it cheap enough for a consumer
# gate. crysta's tools/ci/edi-verification.sh invokes this task by name.
verification-parity-tests = { cmd = [
    "python", "-m", "pytest", "tests/system/py/test_e02_fullprof_parity.py", "-q",
], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# The marker-filtered `per-pr-tests` task is RETIRED with the `heavy` marker — the named groups
# below are the selection surface, and each names tiers, never a runtime predicate. The three
# groups collapse into TWO named for WHEN they run — `quick` (CI on a pull request; the
# review-time run) and `full` (CI on merge; the merge-time run, ONCE after the accept). The
# former local-before-PR group IS quick (nothing runs per commit); selection is unchanged and
# EQUAL between the two.
group-quick = { depends-on = ["quick-tests", "cpp-test"] }
group-full = { depends-on = ["test", "cpp-test"] }
group-nightly-only = { depends-on = ["nightly-only-tests"] }
# Run on its own it builds first, as every app step does: the core the suite's conftest imports and the app,
# in its own environment; app-verify runs it with --skip-deps on its one build.
group-app = { cmd = ["python", "-m", "pytest", "tests/integration/app", "-q"], depends-on = ["core-build", { task = "app-build", environment = "app" }] }
# The packed web app (wasm-build's zip): the given pytest files and the browser driver in each case, in this
# environment (the tests import edi): tools/ci/wasm-check.sh.
wasm-check = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/wasm-check.sh"] }
# The multithread web app's parallel fit: the browser matrix with its speed ratio, and crysta's executed-body witness
# (tools/ci/wasm-parallel-check.sh).
wasm-parallel-check = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/wasm-parallel-check.sh"] }
# The cadence entry points: `verify-quick` — the static checks, the core build, the audit and
# the quick group — runs ONCE before handing to review; `verify-full` (== `verify`, the mount
# `verify:` command and the x-ship gate) runs ONCE when ready to merge, after the accept.
verify-quick = { depends-on = ["check", "format-check", "weakref-policy", "entity-path-check", "tutorial-exclusions", "category-census-check", "core-build", "python-surface-superset", "python-surface-check", "cli-vocabulary-check", "per-pr-audit", "crysta-consumer", "cli-projects", "group-quick", "py-cov-unit", "generated-regions", "app-verify"] }
# Gate the audit: every collected test must have a recorded runtime backing its tier. Collection
# imports `edi._edi`, so without core-build the audit dies with
# `ImportError: edi's compiled extension ... is not importable`. It passed locally and inside
# verify-quick only because core-build runs earlier in those chains; standalone in CI it does not.
per-pr-audit = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/per_pr_runtimes.py"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# ADR-0013: production weak references are prohibited; the capability-class gate.
weakref-policy = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/weakref_policy.py"] }
# ADR-0016: no entity path is composed from a name in edi — in verify-quick,
# verify-full and the CI lint step, so the two gate sets stay equal.
entity-path-check = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/entity_path_convention.py"] }
# ADR-0018: every category has its schema, and the committed census is the generated one —
# in verify-quick, verify-full and the CI lint job's static policy step.
category-census-check = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/category_census.py"] }
# The declared tutorial execution-exclusion gate (edi half).
tutorial-exclusions = { cmd = ["python", "tools/checks/tutorial_execution_exclusions.py"] }
# Re-measure and rewrite the manifest (serial, so per-test numbers are attributable).
per-pr-measure = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/per-pr-measure.sh"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# Gate every region this repo generates into a committed document: re-render each from the
# committed oracle and compare BYTE FOR BYTE. Review-7 F1 was a one-byte drift between the
# generator's output and the committed table that a ledger row asserted was identical; a machine
# comparison fails it inside the lane's own run instead of costing a review round. Renders from
# `oracle.json`, so it needs no diffraction-lib checkout and no built module.
generated-regions = { cmd = ["python", "tests/fixtures/c11_t40_diffraction_lib_reference/generate.py", "--check"] }
# --- coverage ----------------------: package-only (lib/edi), UNIT-tier-only Python coverage
# with a
# `fail_under` declared in pyproject.toml [tool.coverage.report], seeded at today's measured value.
# The former all-tiers `py-cov-report` measured the wrong thing (system/integration reach is not
# unit coverage) and is retired; this runs in both verify chains.
py-cov-unit = { cmd = [
    "python", "-m", "pytest",
    "tests/unit",
    "-q",
    "--cov=edi", "--cov-report=term",
], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# --- the C++ unit tier ---------------------------------------------- One doctest
# binary, built EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL in its own side tree so it never taxes
# `core-build`. In the declared groups (verify-full): the tier now carries test-lane cases under
# tests/unit/cpp/test_*.cpp, so the temporary empty-tier routing exception is over.
# cpp-test.sh still refuses an empty tier rather than passing vacuously, so if every case
# were removed this gate would go red rather than quietly assert nothing.
cpp-test = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/cpp-test.sh"] }
# ADR-0020 §3: the calculation worker and the owner thread under ThreadSanitizer, with crysta built from
# the pinned source under it too (build/tsan). Linux only; the script says so elsewhere.
tsan-worker = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/tsan-worker.sh"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# ADR-0020 §5: run the latency probe ten times and bank this machine's medians with their
# margins (tests/latency-bank.json); `python tools/ci/latency_bank.py --check` is what the ratchet gate calls.
latency-bank = { cmd = ["python", "tools/ci/latency_bank.py", "--run"], depends-on = ["core-build"] }
# The app's gates, each run in the `app` environment (build, lint, format, tests, UI test): a task of this
# environment, so verify-quick / verify-full list it by name and the default environment stays Qt-free. Builds
# once and checks on that build: every check depends on app-build (and group-app on core-build too), and pixi
# runs a dependency the tasks share once per invocation, each task in its own environment's activation (none
# nested, so the app builds under the identity a direct run has, note 19). Every reference names app-build
# with its environment: pixi keys an inherited-environment reference apart from an explicit one and would run
# it twice.
app-verify = { depends-on = [
    "core-build",
    { task = "app-lint", environment = "app" },
    { task = "app-format-check", environment = "app" },
    "group-app",
] }
# LLVM source-based line coverage over the C++ core; gates it on pyproject.toml
# [tool.edi.coverage] cpp_lines_min, seeded at the measured value.
cpp-coverage-unit = { cmd = ["bash", "tools/ci/cpp-coverage-unit.sh"] }
# --- docs ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
docs-build = "mkdocs build --strict"
docs-clean = "rm -rf site"
docs-serve = "mkdocs serve"
# --- the full local gate --------------------------------------------------------------:
# `verify` IS `verify-full` — the merge-time gate, run ONCE after the accept. The wall-clock
# wrapper (a 300 s end-to-end ceiling) is RETIRED with the aggregate suite budget — a whole-run
# total is an aggregate time gate under another name, decided by host variance, and the owner
# ruled that only per-test tier bounds are checked. The P1.14 narrowing is RETIRED with the
# `heavy` marker — quick and full run the same tier selection, so the review-time and
# merge-time runs (and CI-on-PR / CI-on-merge) are equal on TEST selection; what stays
# merge-only is jobs, never tests.
verify = { depends-on = ["verify-full"] }
# `per-pr-audit` runs BEFORE the suite, deliberately. It sat after the suite and pixi stops the
# chain at the first failure, so while the suite was red the audit NEVER EXECUTED - and the
# ruling-58 threshold ratchet shipped inside it was never once run by the gate that owns it. A
# ratchet nobody runs is a ratchet nobody has. Its own prerequisites (`core-build`, so
# `--collect-only` can import edi) still precede it; everything it does not need follows it.:
# `verify-full` is the merge-time FULL chain (the `full` group replaces the former per-commit
# selection; `verify` == `verify-full` — the mount `verify:` command and the x-ship gate, run
# ONCE after the accept). `verify-quick` is the review-time chain.
verify-full = { depends-on = ["check", "format-check", "weakref-policy", "entity-path-check", "tutorial-exclusions", "category-census-check", "core-build", "python-surface-superset", "python-surface-check", "cli-vocabulary-check", "per-pr-audit", "crysta-consumer", "cli-projects", "group-full", "py-cov-unit", "notebook-tests", "generated-regions", "docs-build", "tsan-worker", "app-verify"] }
# The merge-Linux equivalence set: the full chain itself (`verify` now IS the full chain,
# so the two are one). `tools/ci/local-ci.sh` runs this.
merge-tasks = { depends-on = ["verify-full"] }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# One part of the system tier, for CI's parallel system jobs:
#
#   pixi run system-tests-part <part> [<parts>]      part 1..parts, parts 3 by default
#
# pytest-split assigns every test of tests/system to exactly one part, balancing the parts by the
# recorded durations in $EDI_TEST_DURATIONS (default build/test-durations.json). A test with no
# recorded time counts as the average, so a new test needs no list kept by hand; with no file at
# all the parts are balanced by count. The run writes its own tests' durations to
# build/test-durations-<part>.json, which CI keeps as an artifact and merges on main
# (tools/ci/merge_test_durations.py).
#
# The files of the `nightly-only` group in tests/test-groups.json are left out unless EDI_RUN_NIGHTLY_ONLY=true,
# which only the nightly schedule sets: they build an app of their own.
set -euo pipefail
part="${1:?usage: system-tests-part <part> [<parts>]}"
parts="${2:-3}"
case "$part$parts" in *[!0-9]*) echo "system-tests-part: part and parts must be whole numbers" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
[ "$part" -ge 1 ] && [ "$part" -le "$parts" ] || { echo "system-tests-part: part $part is not in 1..$parts" >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p build
recorded="${EDI_TEST_DURATIONS:-build/test-durations.json}"
own="build/test-durations-$part.json"
if [ -f "$recorded" ]; then cp "$recorded" "$own"; else echo '{}' > "$own"; fi
set --
if [ "${EDI_RUN_NIGHTLY_ONLY:-false}" != true ]; then
  nightly="$(python -c 'import json; print("\n".join(json.load(open("tests/test-groups.json"))["groups"]["nightly-only"]["paths"]))')"
  [ -n "$nightly" ] || { echo "system-tests-part: the nightly-only group names no files" >&2; exit 2; }
  while IFS= read -r path; do set -- "$@" "--ignore=$path"; done <<< "$nightly"
fi
exec python -m pytest tests/system -q "$@" \
    --splits "$parts" --group "$part" --splitting-algorithm least_duration \
    --durations-path "$own" --store-durations

#!/usr/bin/env bash # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause # Acquire crysta as a CMake package: the pinned, prebuilt C++ SDK crysta's CI built and tested (edi # ADR-0017). No path compiles crysta. # # The pin is pixi.toml's CRYSTA_SDK_TAG / CRYSTA_SDK_SHA256 for this platform. tools/ci/crysta_sdk.py # reuses build/crysta-sdk/-/ when its recorded sha256 matches the pin, else downloads the # release asset over the REST API (curl; no `gh` on the CI fleet), verifies the sha256, unpacks it and # checks its toolchain fingerprint against this environment's pixi.lock (I25), refusing before anything # configures. It prints the provenance line the CI evidence binds: # crysta: using SDK build- tree sha256 platform

# # The prefix every consumer reads (build/crysta-prefix, suffixed per pixi environment as before) is a # link to the SDK, and `.crysta-sha` in it records the SDK's source commit. (The corpus and reference # source edi's tests read, which the SDK does not carry, are fetched by tools/ci/crysta-src.sh.) # # CRYSTA_SDK_DIR an unpacked SDK to use instead of the pin: crysta's edi-verification candidate # or a diagnostic. Same fingerprint check; its own prefix # (build/crysta-consumer-prefix) so the pinned records are never touched. The # consumer configuration's source (corpus, reference) is CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC, # which must then be the SDK's source tree at its commit. # CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC refused without CRYSTA_SDK_DIR: a crysta working tree is never compiled here. set -euo pipefail ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)" # edi repo root cd "$ROOT" # One prefix per pixi environment; the default keeps the unsuffixed paths every core consumer reads, # and app-build.sh derives the same suffix (keep in step). ENV_NAME="${PIXI_ENVIRONMENT_NAME:-$(basename "${CONDA_PREFIX:-default}")}" case "$ENV_NAME" in default | "") ENV_SUFFIX="" ;; *) ENV_SUFFIX="-$ENV_NAME" ;; esac # Seam 12: the one platform mapping in this script — the pixi platform the task runs on (PIXI_PLATFORM; the app # environment's linux-64-app is linux-64), else the runner's labels, else the host. case "${PIXI_PLATFORM:-${RUNNER_OS:-$(uname -s)}-${RUNNER_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}}" in linux-64 | linux-64-app | Linux-X64 | Linux-x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-64 ;; osx-arm64 | macOS-ARM64 | Darwin-arm64) PLATFORM=osx-arm64 ;; *) echo "ERROR: no crysta SDK is built for ${PIXI_PLATFORM:-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)} (edi ADR-0017: linux-64, osx-arm64)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac # The prefix is shared mutable state: a pytest worker never writes it (core-build's lock covers its callers). [ -z "${PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER:-}" ] || { echo "REFUSING: pytest worker ${PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER} may not write the crysta prefix" >&2; exit 1; } # The prefix and the SDK cache are written under edi's producer lock (tools/ci/producer-lock.sh). . "$ROOT/tools/ci/producer-lock.sh"; edi_producer_lock "$ROOT" if [ -n "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ]; then PREFIX="$ROOT/build/crysta-consumer-prefix$ENV_SUFFIX" OUT="$(python tools/ci/crysta_sdk.py check --sdk "$CRYSTA_SDK_DIR" --platform "$PLATFORM")" elif [ -n "${CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC:-}" ]; then echo "ERROR: CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC=$CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC without CRYSTA_SDK_DIR — edi never compiles crysta (ADR-0017); pack an SDK (crysta: pixi run -e cpp-ci sdk-pack) and set CRYSTA_SDK_DIR" >&2 exit 1 else PREFIX="$ROOT/build/crysta-prefix$ENV_SUFFIX" OUT="$(python tools/ci/crysta_sdk.py fetch --platform "$PLATFORM")" fi # ONE provenance line per CI job (RUNNER_TEMP is job-scoped) — a later call linking the same SDK is silent, one # linking a different SDK logs again, so a contradiction stays two lines the reader refuses. LINE="${OUT%%$'\n'*}" SEEN="${RUNNER_TEMP:+$RUNNER_TEMP/crysta-sdk-line}" # crysta: using SDK build- tree ... if [ -z "$SEEN" ] || [ "$(cat "$SEEN" 2>/dev/null)" != "$LINE" ]; then echo "$LINE"; [ -z "$SEEN" ] || printf '%s\n' "$LINE" >"$SEEN"; fi SDK="${OUT##*$'\n'}" SHA="$(python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["source_sha"])' "$SDK/share/crysta-sdk/manifest.json")" # The prefix is edi's own directory linking the SDK's top-level entries, so the SDK itself — a cache entry, # or a caller's CRYSTA_SDK_DIR — is never written; `.crysta-sha` records the SDK's source commit here. # F02: a prefix already linking exactly this SDK is left as it is — a reader building against it is never disturbed. want="$(for e in "$SDK"/*; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$e")" "$e"; done; echo "$SHA")" have="$(cd "$PREFIX" 2>/dev/null && for f in *; do printf '%s %s\n' "$f" "$(readlink "$f")"; done; cat .crysta-sha 2>/dev/null)" || have="" if [ "$want" != "$have" ]; then rm -rf "$PREFIX" && mkdir -p "$PREFIX" for entry in "$SDK"/*; do ln -s "$entry" "$PREFIX/$(basename "$entry")"; done printf '%s\n' "$SHA" >"$PREFIX/.crysta-sha" fi if [ -n "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ] && [ -n "${CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC:-}" ]; then # The consumer configuration's source (corpus, reference) is the caller's tree: the SDK's own commit. live="$(git -C "$CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none)" [ "$live" = "$SHA" ] || { echo "ERROR: CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC is at $live but the SDK was built from $SHA" >&2; exit 1; } fi echo "crysta::crysta ($SHA) from the SDK at $SDK, linked as $PREFIX"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Configure + build the edi C++ core (Release). From the core links crysta::crysta, so first acquire
# the pinned crysta SDK as a CMake package at build/crysta-prefix (ADR-0003, ADR-0017), then
# configure edi with that prefix on CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH. Skips cleanly while no CMake tree exists, so
# CI stays green on the pre-code skeleton.
set -euo pipefail
if [ -f CMakeLists.txt ]; then SRC=.; elif [ -f core/CMakeLists.txt ]; then SRC=core; else
  echo "no CMake tree yet — skeleton pass"; exit 0
fi
ROOT="$(pwd)"

# ⛔ ONE PRODUCER AT A TIME. The crysta prefix and the edi build dir are SHARED mutable state: two
# concurrent builds interleave their writes into the same tree, and the loser observes a
# half-installed prefix — a failure that reads as a source defect and is not reproducible. A
# pytest worker that shells out to this script is exactly that second producer. `flock` serialises
# them: the second waits rather than corrupting the first, and the wait is bounded so a stale
# holder fails loudly instead of hanging the gate forever. A pytest WORKER may not enter the
# producer at all. Serialising would only make the second worker wait for a build it must not have
# started: the suite's job is to consume the built artifact, not to produce it, and a worker that
# builds races every other worker's imports. Refused by name so the cause is legible instead of
# surfacing as a corrupt-prefix import error.
if [ -n "${PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER:-}" ]; then
  echo "REFUSING: pytest worker ${PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER} may not enter the shared core build." >&2
  echo "The core is built once, before the suite runs; a worker that builds races every other" >&2
  echo "worker's imports against a half-installed prefix. Run 'pixi run core-build' first." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# CRYSTA_SDK_DIR builds build/ci-consumer, which every runtime reader selects only by the ONE consumer selector
# (lib/edi/__init__.py, verification, python_surface_superset, crysta-consumer.sh), so a candidate build without
# it would be followed by an import of the ordinary build/ci. Refused before any write.
if [ -n "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ] && ! { [ -n "${EDI_USE_CONSUMER_BUILD:-}" ] \
  || [ "${CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC:-}" = "hidden-surface-control" ] \
  || { [ -n "${CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC:-}" ] && [ -f "${CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC}/CMakeLists.txt" ]; }; }; then
  echo "REFUSING: CRYSTA_SDK_DIR builds build/ci-consumer, which no runtime reader selects without EDI_USE_CONSUMER_BUILD or CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC (the SDK's source tree)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# `.lock.d`, not `.lock`: the OLD flock implementation left a regular FILE at the bare path,
# and `mkdir` can never succeed against one — a checkout carrying that legacy file would wait
# out the whole deadline and then refuse, forever. Measured on this box, in both repos. A
# distinct directory-shaped path makes the migration inert instead of fatal.
BUILD_LOCK="$ROOT/build/.core-build.lock.d"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$BUILD_LOCK")"
# The lock is `mkdir`, NOT `flock`, and it is NOT taken via `exec`. Two defects were fused here:
# `flock` is util-linux and macOS ships none (conda-forge has no osx-arm64 flock either, so it
# cannot be pinned the way bash and coreutils were) — so `command -v flock` failed on the macOS
# leg and the lock VANISHED, with no else branch and no message. And `exec` REPLACES this shell,
# so nothing downstream could ever have reported it. `mkdir` is atomic on POSIX and needs no
# re-exec, which is what makes the failure sayable at all.
BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S="${EDI_CORE_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S:-1800}"
_waited=0
until mkdir "$BUILD_LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  if [ "$_waited" -ge "$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S" ]; then
    echo "REFUSING: another core build has held $BUILD_LOCK for ${BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S}s." >&2
    echo "Two concurrent builds interleave writes into one prefix and the loser observes a" >&2
    echo "half-installed tree. If no build is running, an earlier one was killed: remove" >&2
    echo "$BUILD_LOCK." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
  _waited=$((_waited + 1))
done
# Released on ANY exit, so an ordinary run never leaves it behind; a killed run does, and the
# bounded wait above then refuses loudly by name rather than hanging the gate forever.
trap 'rm -f "$BUILD_LOCK/owner"; rmdir "$BUILD_LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
# Build-crysta.sh below runs inside THIS acquisition — a token only this holder wrote, never a path
export EDI_PRODUCER_LOCK_HELD="$$.$RANDOM.$RANDOM"; printf '%s\n' "$EDI_PRODUCER_LOCK_HELD" >"$BUILD_LOCK/owner"
# Acquire crysta as a CMake package, inside this producer lock: the pinned SDK (ADR-0017), or
# CRYSTA_SDK_DIR's candidate. Needs the crysta link deps in the env (eigen/sleef/openmp) — see pixi.toml.
bash tools/ci/build-crysta.sh
# The linked commit's corpus and reference source for edi's tests (fetched, never built).
bash tools/ci/crysta-src.sh
# A consumer job restores the artifact `native · <platform>` built once for this run, each bound field
# and every restored byte checked against it, and compiles nothing.
if [ "${EDI_NATIVE_ARTIFACT:-}" = 1 ]; then
  python tools/ci/edi_native.py restore; exit $?  # never exec: the EXIT trap releases the lock
fi
# In the crysta->edi consumer-contract direction the crysta package is the candidate SDK in its own
# prefix, so edi configures against THAT prefix and into its own build tree. Keeping the two apart is
# what lets a consumer run and edi's own pinned build coexist in one checkout without either
# invalidating the other.
if [ -n "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ]; then
  CRYSTA_PREFIX="$ROOT/build/crysta-consumer-prefix"
  EDI_BUILD_DIR=build/ci-consumer
else
  CRYSTA_PREFIX="$ROOT/build/crysta-prefix"
  EDI_BUILD_DIR=build/ci
fi
# The declared deployment target on every configure, as for crysta above, so edi's objects and
# its link agree with the crysta objects they link.
cmake -S "$SRC" -B "$EDI_BUILD_DIR" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$CRYSTA_PREFIX" \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET="${MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET:-}"
cmake --build "$EDI_BUILD_DIR" -j
# Further targets in this same tree, under this lock (the C++ tier's edi_tests).
[ -z "${EDI_CORE_TARGETS:-}" ] || cmake --build "$EDI_BUILD_DIR" --target ${EDI_CORE_TARGETS} -j
# Review-7 F7: tie provenance to the edi artifact actually LINKED. The prefix stamp and source
# record are mutable across resolves; this record names the crysta the just-built edi contains,
# and downstream consumers select it instead of re-reading whatever a later resolve left behind.
cp "$CRYSTA_PREFIX/.crysta-sha" "$EDI_BUILD_DIR/.crysta-linked-sha"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Edi's C++ unit gate — the one doctest binary, built in core-build's tree.
#
# The crysta precedent (tools/ci/cpp-test.sh there) shards a 112-case suite off a committed
# cost table. edi's tier is ONE binary with no cost table and no derivation, so this is the
# proportionate port: configure, build the EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL target, run it once. Sharding
# arrives here if and when the case count makes it pay, not before.
#
# This is the ONE script the pixi task and any CI surface invoke, so the surfaces cannot
# diverge (the crysta _lto_correctness.sh discipline).
#
# Fails closed, and the two refusals below are the point: a C++ tier that reports success
# because it has no cases, or because doctest is missing from the env, asserts nothing.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

# The tier runs in core-build's own tree — build/ci, or build/ci-consumer for a candidate SDK — whose
# configure is identical to the separate build/tests this used to configure. The edi_tests target is built
# there by core-build, under its producer lock; a consumer job instead restores the tree `native ·
# <platform>` built once (EDI_NATIVE_ARTIFACT=1) and configures nothing.
if [ -n "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ]; then TREE=build/ci-consumer; else TREE=build/ci; fi
EDI_CORE_TARGETS=edi_tests bash tools/ci/core-build.sh

# The target is defined only when doctest resolves AND tests/unit/cpp/test_*.cpp is non-empty
# (core/CMakeLists.txt). Absent either, the tier cannot assert anything — refuse loudly rather
# than exit 0 on a vacuous run.
case_files=$(cat "$TREE/edi_tests_case_files.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${case_files:-0}" -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "cpp-test: no edi_tests target — either doctest is absent from the env or the tier" >&2
    echo "has no cases (tests/unit/cpp/test_*.cpp). An empty C++ tier is a refusal, not a pass." >&2
    exit 1
fi

log="$TREE/edi_tests.log"
status=0
"$TREE/core/edi_tests" >"$log" 2>&1 || status=$?
cat "$log"
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "cpp-test: edi_tests exited $status" >&2
    exit "$status"
fi

# Non-vacuity: doctest exits 0 on "no test cases ran", so the reported count is what proves
# the binary did work. Parsed from doctest's own summary line.
ran=$(grep -oE 'test cases: *[0-9]+' "$log" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1)
if [ "${ran:-0}" -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "cpp-test: edi_tests reported ${ran:-no} test cases — a green run that asserted nothing" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "cpp-test: $ran C++ unit case(s) green"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# edi's crysta pin reader, its currency check and their remote helpers (edi ADR-0017). Run directly, it reads
# the committed pin and outputs the pinned sha: the
# `changes` job runs it once per workflow run, for the record the CI evidence reads. The
# `pin currency` job runs it with --currency (crysta_currency, below), the one required check on the pin itself
# (owner, 2026-10-01): it reports a stale pin, and fails only when the pin or the answer cannot be read. edi
# never compiles crysta: build-crysta.sh takes a prebuilt SDK, the pinned one or, in a paired run whose pin is
# stale, the paired crysta branch head's (crysta_paired_head, below), and crysta-src.sh sources the remote
# helpers to fetch that build's source.
#
# Branch lookups use `git ls-remote` over the authenticated URL (the self-hosted runners have no
# `gh`), so a successful answer also proves the token reads crysta. A branch proven ABSENT, or one whose head
# has landed on crysta main, leaves the PR unpaired (a branch that merely exists pairs nothing); a lookup
# ERROR refuses by name, since a branch that could not be resolved is never read as absent.
#
# Remote steps: an auth or `Repository not found` failure is retried, 3 attempts with 5 s and 15 s
# backoff, each failure logging the repositories the token grants; any other failure is final.
#
#   bash tools/ci/crysta-source.sh                -> prints the pinned sha; in CI also `sha=<sha>` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT
#   bash tools/ci/crysta-source.sh --currency     -> reports whether the pin is current; exit 1 only when the
#                                                    pin or the answer cannot be read
#   bash tools/ci/crysta-source.sh --paired-head  -> prints the paired crysta branch's head, or an empty line
#   bash tools/ci/crysta-source.sh --paired-commit <sha>  -> exit 0 when <sha> is a commit of the paired crysta
#                                                    branch that crysta main lacks; 1 when it is not; 2 unread

CRYSTA_REPO="enhantica/crysta"
CRYSTA_PUBLIC_URL="https://github.com/$CRYSTA_REPO"
: "${CRYSTA_SRC:=$HOME/Development/github.com/enhantica/crysta}"

# The URL every remote step uses: the public URL, authenticated with the CI token when one is passed
# (named in the log, never echoed by value — see _crysta_redact).
crysta_url() {
  if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    printf 'https://x-access-token:%s@github.com/%s' "$GITHUB_TOKEN" "$CRYSTA_REPO"
  else
    printf '%s' "$CRYSTA_PUBLIC_URL"
  fi
}

_crysta_redact() {  # never a token by value, even in git's own words
  local text="$1"
  [ -z "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ] || text="${text//${GITHUB_TOKEN}/***}"
  printf '%s' "$text"
}

_crysta_granted() {  # the repositories the minted token reads, listed with curl
  local out rc=0
  out="$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    https://api.github.com/installation/repositories 2>&1)" || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "build-crysta: the token's grants could not be listed (curl exit $rc): $(_crysta_redact "$out")" >&2
  else
    echo "build-crysta: the token grants: $(printf '%s' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"full_name": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | tr '\n' ' ')" >&2
  fi
}

# crysta_remote <step> <git args...>: run one remote git step with the bounded auth retry. The output
# lands in CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT; the return code is git's last. `.extraheader` is cleared because
# actions/checkout's persisted repo-scoped header would override the URL credential (PR54 run 3).
crysta_remote() {
  local step="$1" attempt=1 rc
  shift
  while :; do
    rc=0
    CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT="$(git -c http.https://github.com/.extraheader= "$@" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && return 0
    case "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT" in
      *"Repository not found"* | *"Authentication failed"* | *"could not read Username"* | \
        *"Invalid username or password"* | *"returned error: 401"* | *"returned error: 403"*) ;;
      *) return "$rc" ;;
    esac
    echo "build-crysta: $step attempt $attempt/3 failed (rc=$rc): $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT")" >&2
    _crysta_granted
    [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ] || return "$rc"
    if [ "$attempt" -eq 1 ]; then sleep 5; else sleep 15; fi
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  done
}

# crysta_branch_head <branch>: the same-named crysta branch's head in CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD, or empty when the
# branch is proven ABSENT; returns 1 (the cause printed) on a lookup error. Read with
# `git ls-remote` over the authenticated URL (no `gh`): success proves crysta is readable. The
# answer is accepted only as exactly one line `<40-hex sha><TAB>refs/heads/<branch>`, or as no line at all
# (absent). Anything else — a failure, a second line, a line naming any other ref (a tag or another branch
# with that name included), or a malformed line — is a lookup error, never read as absence.
crysta_branch_head() {
  CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD=""
  local want="refs/heads/$1" lines="" found="" count=0 line bad=0
  if ! crysta_remote "branch lookup" ls-remote "$(crysta_url)" "$want"; then
    echo "crysta-resolution: the crysta branch lookup for '$1' failed: $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT") — refusing: a branch that cannot be resolved is never replaced by crysta main" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  lines="$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT"
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^([0-9a-f]{40})$'\t'(.+)$ ]] && [ "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" = "$want" ]; then
      count=$((count + 1))
      found="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    else
      bad=1
    fi
  done <<<"$lines"
  if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ] || [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then
    echo "crysta-resolution: the crysta branch lookup for '$1' gave an answer other than exactly $want: $(_crysta_redact "$lines") — refusing" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD="$found"
}

# crysta_pin <pixi.toml> <label>: prints the one build that file pins (THE pin contract,
# tools/ci/crysta_sdk.py, decides it; nothing here reads pixi.toml). Returns 1, the cause printed, unless every
# platform pins one build.
crysta_pin() {
  local root shas
  root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
  shas="$(python3 "$root/tools/ci/crysta_sdk.py" pins "$1" | sort -u | grep .)" || shas=""
  if [ -z "$shas" ] || [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$shas" | wc -l)" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "crysta-pin: $2 pins ${shas:-no} crysta build(s); every platform pins one build" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$shas"
}

# crysta_landed <sha> [ref]: 0 when <sha> has landed on crysta main — a main commit, or a paired PR head squashed
# onto main, whose tree a main commit carries. The commit is read through [ref]: its retained build-<sha> tag by
# default, or the branch ref whose head it is. 1 when it has not landed; 2, the cause printed, when crysta, that
# ref or the commit through it could not be read. The clone fetches commits only (no trees, no blobs).
crysta_landed() {
  local clone rc=2 anc=0 tree trees ref="${2:-refs/tags/build-$1}" what="${2:-build-$1}"  # review-18 F03: only a history read in full answers 1
  clone="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/crysta-currency.XXXXXX")"  # the job's temp: a cancel cannot strand it
  if ! crysta_remote "main clone" clone -q --bare --filter=tree:0 --single-branch --branch main "$(crysta_url)" "$clone/c"; then
    echo "crysta-currency: crysta main could not be read: $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT")" >&2
  else
    git -C "$clone/c" merge-base --is-ancestor "$1" main 2>/dev/null || anc=$?
    if [ "$anc" -eq 0 ]; then
      rc=0  # ancestry, never presence: a partial clone fetches any missing commit on demand
    elif [ "$anc" -ne 1 ]; then  # review-20 F02: any lookup error is red (gate 9), whatever a later lookup finds
      echo "crysta-currency: the ancestry of $1 could not be read (merge-base exit $anc)" >&2
    elif ! crysta_remote "${2:+branch }${2:-build tag}" -C "$clone/c" fetch -q origin "$ref:$ref"; then
      echo "crysta-currency: $what could not be read: $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT")" >&2
    elif ! tree="$(git -C "$clone/c" rev-parse "$1^{tree}")" || ! trees="$(git -C "$clone/c" log --format=%T main)"; then
      echo "crysta-currency: $what's tree or crysta main's history could not be read" >&2
    elif grep -qxF "$tree" <<<"$trees"; then
      rc=0  # a paired head squashed onto main: main carries its tree
    else
      rc=1  # read in full: neither an ancestor of main nor a tree main carries
    fi
  fi
  rm -rf "$clone"
  return "$rc"
}

# crysta_paired_head: is this run paired? A pull request, or a dispatched run, is paired when its
# branch has a same-named crysta branch whose head has NOT landed on crysta main. Sets CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH to the
# run's branch when that crysta branch exists, and CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD to its head when the run is paired; both
# are empty otherwise. Returns 1, the cause printed, on any lookup error: an unread answer is never "unpaired".
# One rule answers the currency check below and the build (crysta_sdk.py fetch, through --paired-head).
crysta_paired_head() {
  local branch="" landed=0
  CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH="" CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD=""
  case "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME:-}" in
    pull_request) branch="${GITHUB_HEAD_REF:-}" ;;
    workflow_dispatch) branch="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}" ;;
  esac
  [ -n "$branch" ] || return 0
  crysta_branch_head "$branch" || return 1
  [ -n "$CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD" ] || return 0
  CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH="$branch"
  crysta_landed "$CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD" "refs/heads/$branch" || landed=$?
  [ "$landed" -le 1 ] || return 1
  [ "$landed" -eq 0 ] || CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD="$CRYSTA_BRANCH_HEAD"
}

# crysta_paired_commit <sha>: is <sha> a commit this paired run may have built? That is the paired crysta
# branch's head, or an earlier commit of that branch that crysta main lacks: the head a job of the same run found
# before the branch moved on. 0 when it is; 1 when the run is unpaired or the commit is not on the branch or has
# landed; 2, the cause printed, when the answer cannot be read. The clone fetches commits only.
crysta_paired_commit() {
  local clone rc=2 on_branch=0 on_main=0 ref
  crysta_paired_head || return 2
  [ -n "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD" ] || return 1
  [ "$1" != "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD" ] || return 0
  ref="refs/heads/$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH"
  clone="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/crysta-paired.XXXXXX")"
  if ! crysta_remote "main clone" clone -q --bare --filter=tree:0 --single-branch --branch main "$(crysta_url)" "$clone/c"; then
    echo "crysta-paired: crysta main could not be read: $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT")" >&2
  elif ! crysta_remote "branch" -C "$clone/c" fetch -q origin "$ref:$ref"; then
    echo "crysta-paired: crysta branch '$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH' could not be read: $(_crysta_redact "$CRYSTA_REMOTE_OUT")" >&2
  else
    git -C "$clone/c" merge-base --is-ancestor "$1" "$ref" 2>/dev/null || on_branch=$?
    git -C "$clone/c" merge-base --is-ancestor "$1" main 2>/dev/null || on_main=$?
    if [ "$on_branch" -gt 1 ] || [ "$on_main" -gt 1 ]; then
      rc=1  # the commit is not in crysta at all: not a commit of the branch
    elif [ "$on_branch" -eq 0 ] && [ "$on_main" -eq 1 ]; then
      rc=0
    else
      rc=1
    fi
  fi
  rm -rf "$clone"
  return "$rc"
}

# _crysta_stale <what>: report a stale pin and the fix; in CI the same report is a warning on the run.
_crysta_stale() {
  echo "crysta-currency: $1" >&2
  echo "crysta-currency: the stale pin is reported, not refused: the final CI evidence and the merge refuse it" >&2
  [ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" != true ] || echo "::warning title=stale crysta pin::$1"
}

# crysta_currency (I10; edi ADR-0017): is
# the committed pin current? Paired (crysta_paired_head), the current pin is that crysta branch's head. Unpaired,
# it has landed on crysta main (crysta_landed) or is the pin on edi main. A pin that is not current is STALE: it
# is reported, with the fix, and the answer is still 0. A task's crysta branch moves with every crysta commit, so
# a job that failed on each of those rows said nothing new; a paired run builds the branch head whatever the pin
# says (crysta_sdk.py fetch); the final CI evidence counts an edi run only when the SDK it built is its pin and the
# paired crysta pull request's head; and the merge guard refuses a pin that has not landed. Returns 1, the cause
# printed, on a pin that cannot be read and on any lookup error: an unread answer is never current.
crysta_currency() {
  local root pin main_pin landed=0
  root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
  pin="$(crysta_pin "$root/pixi.toml" pixi.toml)" || return 1
  crysta_paired_head || return 1
  if [ -n "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD" ] && [ "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD" = "$pin" ]; then
    echo "crysta-currency: paired with crysta branch '$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH', whose head build-$pin is the pin"
    return 0
  elif [ -n "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD" ]; then
    _crysta_stale "crysta branch '$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH' is at $CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD but edi pins build-$pin — re-pin: pixi run crysta-sdk-pin $CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD"
    return 0
  elif [ -n "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH" ]; then
    echo "crysta-currency: crysta branch '$CRYSTA_PAIRED_BRANCH' carries nothing crysta main lacks, so this pull request is unpaired"
  fi
  crysta_landed "$pin" || landed=$?
  if [ "$landed" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "crysta-currency: unpaired; the pin build-$pin has landed on crysta main"
    return 0
  elif [ "$landed" -ne 1 ]; then
    return 1
  fi
  if ! git -C "$root" fetch -q --depth=1 origin main; then
    echo "crysta-currency: edi main could not be read — refusing" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  main_pin="$(crysta_pin <(git -C "$root" show FETCH_HEAD:pixi.toml) "edi main's pixi.toml" 2>/dev/null)" || main_pin=""
  if [ "$main_pin" = "$pin" ]; then
    echo "crysta-currency: unpaired; the pin build-$pin is edi main's"
    return 0
  fi
  _crysta_stale "unpaired, and build-$pin has neither landed on crysta main nor is edi main's pin (${main_pin:+build-}${main_pin:-none}) — re-pin: pixi run crysta-sdk-pin <a crysta main sha>"
  return 0
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  set -euo pipefail
  if [ "${1:-}" = --currency ]; then
    crysta_currency
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "${1:-}" = --paired-head ]; then
    crysta_paired_head
    echo "$CRYSTA_PAIRED_HEAD"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "${1:-}" = --paired-commit ]; then
    crysta_paired_commit "${2:?a crysta sha}" && exit 0 || exit $?
  fi
  CRYSTA_PIN="$(crysta_pin "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)/pixi.toml" pixi.toml)"
  echo "crysta: pinned SDK build-$CRYSTA_PIN" >&2   # The effective pin the CI evidence reads
  echo "$CRYSTA_PIN"
  if [ -n "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}" ]; then
    printf 'sha=%s\n' "$CRYSTA_PIN" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Fetch — never build — the source of the crysta edi links: edi's tests read crysta's fitting corpus and
# reference source at exactly the commit the pinned SDK was built from, and the SDK carries neither. The
# commit is the linked prefix's `.crysta-sha` (tools/ci/build-crysta.sh); the tree lands in
# build/crysta-src with that sha recorded. The consumer configuration (CRYSTA_SDK_DIR) reads its source
# from CRYSTA_CONSUMER_SRC instead, so nothing is fetched for it.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
[ -z "${CRYSTA_SDK_DIR:-}" ] || exit 0
# Build/crysta-src is checked out and cleaned under edi's producer lock (tools/ci/producer-lock.sh).
. "$ROOT/tools/ci/producer-lock.sh"; edi_producer_lock "$ROOT"
SHA="$(cat "$ROOT/build/crysta-prefix/.crysta-sha" 2>/dev/null)" \
  || { echo "ERROR: build/crysta-prefix/.crysta-sha is missing — run tools/ci/build-crysta.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
SRC="$ROOT/build/crysta-src"
if [ "$(cat "$SRC/CRYSTA_SOURCE_SHA" 2>/dev/null)" = "$SHA" ] && [ "$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" = "$SHA" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
# shellcheck source=tools/ci/crysta-source.sh
. "$ROOT/tools/ci/crysta-source.sh"
[ -d "$SRC/.git" ] || git init -q "$SRC"
